title: Domain Adaptive and Generalizable Network Architectures and Training Strategies for Semantic Image Segmentation (DAFormer / HRDA)
mechanism: Training strategies against source overfitting in segmentation: Rare Class Sampling, Thing-Class ImageNet Feature Distance (L2 between bottleneck features and a frozen ImageNet copy on selected classes), lr warmup; plus multi-resolution crops.
adaptation: FD: frozen ImageNet ResNet-34 copy, L2 on layer4 features masked to crack and inactive pixels. RCS: sample cells by rarest class present (temperature 0.01-0.1) so the 42 inactive cells and BMRK crack cells appear more. Multi-res crops left to D22.
evidence: DAFormer and HRDA improve UDA and DG segmentation SOTA by more than 10 mIoU on 5 benchmarks (abstract); per-strategy ablation numbers not retrieved.
min_experiment: Arms FD and FD+RCS vs SUP100-PF, seeds 5-9. Metric: test inactive IoU, E1 inactive IoU, test crack relF1@2. Kill if inactive IoU gain < +0.02 on test and E1 not better.
prior_overlap: none. Feature-space preservation and class-frequency sampling never run (long-tail methods listed as never tried).

alt_notes.adaptation: FD: frozen ImageNet ResNet-34, L2 on layer4 features masked to crack + inactive pixels. RCS: sample whole cells by class frequency (temperature 0.01 to 0.1) over 42 inactive and 209 crack cells; whole-cell input keeps all area reachable.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + FD, PF + RCS, PF + both, 5 seeds. Baseline: SUP100-PF. Metric: inactive IoU (test, E1), BMRK inactive IoU, crack relF1@2. Kill: inactive IoU gain < 0.02 on test and E1.
